note: Embedded Content defines an embedded_content plugin type (annotation @EmbeddedContent, base EmbeddedContentPluginBase, Plugin/EmbeddedContent namespace, build()+isInline()) and embedded_content_button config entities (config name embedded_content.button.<id>, config_prefix 'button', settings: icon/label_singular/submit_button_text/modal_title/conditions/dialog_settings). Each button becomes a CKEditor 5 toolbar item embeddedContent__<id>; the embedded_content text filter renders <embedded-content data-plugin-id data-plugin-config> tags on output. Permissions: administer embedded content + dynamic 'use <button_id> embedded content button'. Ships zero concrete plugins by default. Medium cases seed a known button config entity and the agent reads its settings. Hard cases create a button config entity and enable the embedded_content filter on a new text format, verified against live config. Execution is done through config entities (buttons, filter format) rather than authoring a PHP plugin (which would require a throwaway module on this shared site).

evals.prompt: In the embedded_content Drupal module, how do I define a new embeddable component in code? Which annotation, base class and namespace do I use, and which methods are required?
evals.expected_output: Create a class in src/Plugin/EmbeddedContent/ annotated @EmbeddedContent(id, label) that extends EmbeddedContentPluginBase and implements EmbeddedContentInterface. Implement build() (render array) and isInline() (bool); optionally defaultConfiguration(), buildConfigurationForm(), massageFormValues(), getAttachments().

evals.prompt: How do editors actually insert an embedded_content component into CKEditor 5, and what has to be enabled on the text format for it to work — without giving editors raw HTML permission?
evals.expected_output: Create an Embedded content button, add its CKEditor 5 toolbar item (embeddedContent__<button_id>) to the format's toolbar, and enable the 'Embedded content' filter on that text format. The CKEditor plugin declares the <embedded-content> elements, so no extra allowed-HTML/raw-HTML permission is needed.

evals.prompt: What permission controls whether a user can use a particular embedded_content button, and how is it named?
evals.expected_output: There is a dynamic per-button permission named 'use <button_id> embedded content button' (e.g. 'use default embedded content button'), generated by EmbeddedContentPermissions. Managing buttons themselves uses the 'administer embedded content' permission.

evals.prompt: This site has an embedded_content button config entity with id 'ec_known'. Inspect the live configuration and report the modal title configured for that button.
evals.expected_output: The button config entity embedded_content.button.ec_known has settings.modal_title = 'EC Known Modal'.

evals.prompt: For the embedded_content button 'ec_known' configured on this site, inspect the running configuration and report the singular label (label_singular) it uses for the content being embedded.

On this Drupal site, use the embedded_content module to create a new Embedded content button with machine id 'ec_task', label 'EC Task', and a singular content name (label_singular) of 'component'. Save it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create an embedded_content_button config entity (embedded_content.button.ec_task) with label 'EC Task' and settings.label_singular = 'component'. Verify checks the entity exists with that label and label_singular.

evals.prompt: I need a new text format on my site called 'ec_task_format' where the embedded_content module's component embedding works. Create that text format and turn on the 'Embedded content' filter for it, then save.
evals.expected_output: Create a filter_format 'ec_task_format' with the embedded_content filter enabled (filters.embedded_content.status = true) and save. Verify checks the format exists and its embedded_content filter status is true.
